## Summary

Sueppel (macro-research aggregator) signals a new quantitative-finance working paper: *"A Rough Instantaneous Squared VIX Model for Term Structure and Option Pricing."* The paper's proposal, from the abstract:

- **RISVIX**: introduces **fractional memory** (roughness) into the conventional Markovian squared-VIX framework — the "rough volatility" idea applied directly to the instantaneous squared VIX, rather than only to the spot variance.
- **Term structure with memory**: explicit representation of the VIX term structure governed by **Mittag-Leffler decay** (the fractional-memory generalization of exponential mean reversion).
- **Pricing**: semi-closed-form VIX option formula via an affine **Fourier-Laplace transform**.
- **Two-step calibration**: estimate memory parameter, mean reversion, and date-specific initial states from VIX **term-structure indices first**, then calibrate remaining distributional parameters to **VIX option prices**.
- **Results** (daily VIX term-structure indices + VIX option quotes, Jan 2018 – Jun 2025): beats the Markovian benchmark on term-structure fit — larger gains in **elevated-volatility periods** and for the curve's **slope and curvature**; out-of-sample option pricing improves with **MSE −13.06% / MAE −6.33%**, largest at **shorter maturities and high-VIX states**. Also improves on recent-literature benchmarks to varying degrees.

## Why it matters

- Directly adjacent to the desk's VIX thread ([[2026-11-13-therobotjames-vix-dec-calendar-spread]], the EVRP work in [[2026-11-09-kashin-vix-vix3m-evrp-strategies]]): any desk view that leans on VIX term-structure shape (contango/backwardation trades, calendar spreads, EVRP) benefits if the model used to represent the curve captures memory — this paper claims the standard Markovian curve model systematically misses most exactly when it matters (high-vol states, short maturities).
- The two-step calibration is the practically load-bearing idea: term-structure data is free and dense, option quotes are the expensive/noisy layer — estimating the memory/mean-reversion/initial-state block from the curve first, then fitting distributional params to options, is a reusable pattern even without adopting the full model.
- Skepticism gates: (1) it is a working paper (v1, Nov 2026) — no peer review, no replication yet; (2) fit gains on 2018–2025 include the 2020/2022 vol spikes, so "larger gains in elevated-volatility periods" may be one or two episodes driving the average; (3) in-sample fit ≠ tradable edge — the paper improves *models*, not strategies.

Task filed: pull the full paper and assess whether the fractional-memory term-structure representation changes anything about the desk's VIX calendar/EVRP views.
